objective: Implement and prove one deterministic multi-provider golden audio scenario system across independently governed local, documented-provider, browser/local-companion and manual-external-reference paths without weakening completed AAI rights, capability, entitlement, semantic, availability, binding, permission, sync or capture boundaries.

provider_evidence_refresh.rule: Fresh public review may confirm or narrow existing governed evidence but cannot expand canonical operation rights by inference. AAI-10 tests remain offline even where public integration documentation exists.

canonical_scenario_set.rule: Each golden scenario carries one existing provider-neutral AAI semantic intent plus one governed source/adapter path. The proof compares equivalent canonical intent/source/adapter/rights/capability outcomes, not provider media bytes or audible waveform identity.

live_vs_fixture.result: All five AAI-10 provider/source paths are proven with repository fixtures/test doubles only. No live credential, subscription, provider account, provider network request, authenticated catalog, playback call or content-byte transfer is required or authorized for completion.

persistence.result: No new durable canonical AAI-10 persistence is required. Golden scenarios and deterministic receipts are derived proof/evidence over completed AAI contracts and fixtures.

security_provenance.rule: Credentials, tokens, provider responses, machine-local paths, raw media/content bytes, recordings and raw consent text remain outside committed deterministic evidence. Provider references never imply entitlement, ownership or broader rights.

nonauthorization: live provider authentication or provider network execution
paid provider activation or subscription purchase
provider content acquisition, copying, extraction, caching or rehosting absent independent authority
rights/capability/entitlement promotion by successful reference or control planning
